previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A man with a history of non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy, type I diabetes, COPD, schizophrenia, and chronic crack cocaine use was admitted for acute respiratory distress following progressive dyspnea over 36 hours. He presented with severe shortness of breath, particularly when supine, and was found to have an ejection fraction of 20% on echocardiogram and diffuse bilateral lung opacities on imaging. His respiratory failure was attributed to a combination of acute on chronic systolic heart failure and hypersensitivity pneumonitis likely due to prior crack cocaine use. He was initially managed in the MICU with NIPPV, IV furosemide, and high-dose steroids, then transferred to the general floor. Antibiotics were discontinued after one dose due to lack of infection. His breathing improved rapidly with steroid therapy and diuresis. He was started on a 20-day prednisone taper and required intensified insulin therapy due to steroid-induced hyperglycemia. He was discharged home with his sister, able to ambulate independently on room air, with follow-up arranged for cardiology (AICD evaluation), pulmonary (PFTs and pending hypersensitivity panel), and continuation of his dual diagnosis program for addiction support.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ year old man with schizophrenia, multiple admissions for 
inhaled freebase-cocaine pneumonitis, non-ischemic dilated 
cardiomyopathy with left ventricular ejection fraction of 20% 
who presented in the setting of volume overload secondary to 
dietary indiscretions and was admitted for treatment of acute on 
chronic systolic congestive heart failure.

# Acute on chronic systolic heart failure with a LVEF of 20%:
Upon arrival to the floor ~8am ___, Mr. ___ was in florid 
heart failure. He had 2+ lower extremity edema. His JVD was 
elevated to the angle of the mandible. He his respiratory rate 
was in the low 30's, heavily labored with a saturation of 94% on 
5L facemask. His pulmonary exam notable for diffuse inspiratory 
rales. His BNP was elevated to 5000. He was given IV lasix 40mg 
after which he made approximately 2L of urine. He was 
re-evaluated two hours later and his clinically he appeared to 
be as volume overloaded as before. He was given 80mg of IV lasix 
and he made another 3L of urine. Despite brisk diureisis, his 
respirations were labored with respiratory rates in the ___ and 
oxygen saturation in the 90's on 6L facemask. At that time, he 
noted left sided chest cramps. An EKG was performed which showed 
no dynamic changes concerning for ischemia. His cardiac enzymes 
were negative. Due to concern for impending respiratory failure 
secondary to volume overload, he was transferred to the medical 
ICU for overnight monitoring. In the ICU he received additional 
lasix, but did not require mechanical ventilation. The following 
day, the patient returned to the floor breathing comfortably on 
4L NC. He was actively diuresed with IV lasix to 193 lbs from an 
admission weight of 201 lbs. He responded very well to the 
diuretics and upon discharge had an ambulatory saturation in the 
mid 90's on room air, no JVD, and no lower extremity edema. Of 
note during diuresis his carvedilol was decreased to 3.125mg BID 
from 12.5mg BID secondary to blood pressures in the high ___. 
The patient   
was counseled extensively on the importance of a low sodium diet 
after the patient admitted to eating foods high in salt like 
ramen and BBQ. 

Chronic Issues: 

#Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease: 
Pulmonary function testing from 4 months ago show that Mr. ___ 
has an FEV1 ~50% predicted and a FVC ~65% predicted. These 
values are suggestive of both a component of restrictive and 
obstructive lung disease. Given his previous admissions for 
respiratory failure induced by pneumonia and crack-cocaine 
pneumonitis combined with his chest xray which showed diffuse 
infiltrates concerning for possible pneumonia. The patient was 
treated empirically with antibiotics and steroids upon initial 
presentation. Given his dramatic improvement with lasix and no 
signs of underlying infection (no leukocytosis, left shift) and 
no signs of an acute COPD flare, his steroids and antibiotics 
were discontinued on hospital day two with no adverse affect. No 
changes were made to his outpatient COPD treatment. 

# Diabetes Mellitus: The patient was maintained on his 
outpatient regimen of BID lantus with a sliding scale with blood 
sugars ranging in the 160s to low 200s. 

# HCV: Given his history of HCV, his LFT's were checked upon 
admission and were found to be moderately elevated. His viral 
load was found to be 7 million copies. He is currently being 
followed as an outpatient by Dr. ___. Given his 
cardiopulmonary status he is not currently a candidate for IFN 
per OMR note. 

Medication Changes: 
Lasix INCREASED to 40mg PO BID. 
Carvedilol decreased to 3.25mg BID.
